title: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Incident Review
topics: Root cause: kernel selection + quantized model mismatch
Rollout process and canary policy failures
Action plan: patch, benchmarks, rollout policy changes
summary: Post-incident review of the Nov 18 deploy that caused a multi-region latency spike. We traced to a kernel selection regression for quantized weights on certain GPU drivers plus a misconfigured canary threshold that allowed a bad rollout to proceed. Agreed immediate patch, backfill observability, stricter canary gating, and a follow-up benchmark run before re-enabling aggressive auto-rollouts.

Arjun to add rollout-duration and per-model tail-latency metrics to dashboards - due 2026-11-23

Jordan to update rollout runbook and canary thresholds, communicate to release team - due 2026-11-22

header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 14:00 - 15:04 UTC
Duration: 64 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Priya (PM), Samir (Eng Mgr), Emily (SWE), Jordan (Release), Arjun (Obs), Nina (QA), Cameron (VP Product), Maya (PM), Liam (SRE), Grace (Support)
Notes: internal postmortem / launch readiness check
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, let's get started. We wanted to run through the incident from yesterday's deploy and tie it to our launch readiness checklist. I'll kick off with a quick timeline.
[00:15] Priya: 15:03 UTC we started the canary, 15:07 we started seeing p50 increases, by 15:12 p95 started spiking and by 15:18 errors in eu-west hovered up. The automated rollback didn't trigger.
[00:35] Samir: Quick note \u2014 the rollout system reported healthy for both canary steps, which was misleading. The canary gating was purely error-rate based; tail-latency wasn't in the gate.
[00:50] Emily: Right, and the kernel selection change we shipped in the model runtime had a subtle fallback that selected a quantized kernel path that is incompatible with driver X. It's a timing/regression where the KV cache path mis-handles certain sequence lengths, causing long tails.
[01:10] Liam: To be clear, this only showed up on driver versions 515.x on A100 nodes, not on the older nodes we used in tests, so our bench was green. The fleet mix explains why it slipped by.
[01:35] Priya: So two failure modes: a runtime kernel selection regression + insufficient canary metrics. Any disagreement?
[01:45] Arjun: Yeah, and from observability perspective, we were missing per-model tail-latency and model-kv-cache hit-rate in the default dashboard. We had aggregate P95 but not segmented by model/version.
[02:05] Maya: I noticed the alert thresholds are also wide; the alerting played catch-up. We need earlier detection.
[02:20] Samir: We also had autoscaler instability \u2014 one of the autoscaler controllers flapped under load and didn't add burst nodes fast enough. That exacerbated the tail. It's an infra interaction more than the root cause, but it made impact worse.
[02:45] Emily: The kernel change was intended to optimize attention for longer sequences and quantized weights, but the selection heuristic misclassifies some profiles and picks an experimental kernel. The experimental kernel wasn't tested against the driver matrix.
[03:10] Priya: Can you walk us through the repro?
[03:20] Emily: Sure \u2014 I'll explain. If you run the model with a mixed batch of short and long sequences and the quantize flag on, the allocator can trigger a path where the KV cache pointer offsets are calculated differently; that, combined with a particular driver alignment, leads to repeated recompute and queueing. It's noisy, so it looks like latency spike rather than hard failure.
[03:55] Nina: Is there a simple unit/regression test we can add to catch this?
[04:05] Emily: Yeah, we can add a driver-matrix CI scenario and a mixed-sequence integration test. It will take a bit to run but should be in CI.
[04:25] Jordan: From release side, why didn't the canary catch it? Our canary was a 1% traffic shift with a 10 minute window and error-rate threshold at 1%. If latency goes up but error-rate stays low, it's invisible. We need canary metrics for tail-latency and provision alarms on call-queue length.
[04:50] Priya: Agreed. Proposal: change canary gating to include p99 and model-specific tail metrics and require at least 20% canary coverage before full rollout. Thoughts?
[05:10] Samir: 20% seems reasonable as a conservative start. Also add a manual hold step in the CI pipeline for any kernel-level changes.
[05:25] Arjun: I'll add the p99 per-model to dashboards and create synthetic tests to run during canaries that exercise long-seq paths.
[05:40] Grace: Support saw multiple tickets with similar customer descriptions: "sudden slowness with streaming responses". We should prepare an external note that's honest but not alarming.
[05:55] Priya: I'll draft the external note. Keep it factual: temporary latency increase due to rollout-induced kernel mismatch, resolved, next steps to prevent recurrence.
[06:10] Maya: Any immediate mitigations we did or should do?
[06:20] Jordan: We rolled back the deployment at 15:30 UTC which restored baseline performance, and we disabled the aggressive auto-rollout policy. We should keep that rollback policy change until validation completes.
[06:35] Samir: Also requested an emergency patch from Emily's team to guard the kernel selection — a simple whitelist of kernels by driver version plus a failsafe that forces the older stable kernel if tail-latency exceeds threshold.
[06:55] Emily: I'll open the PR today; it'll include the guard and unit tests. We need to coordinate QA to run the driver matrix tests.
[07:10] Nina: QA can run the driver-matrix daily for this PR; it will add test time but it's necessary.
[07:25] Priya: Okay will someone own the bench run we referenced? We need to simulate fleet mix and driver versions to validate across nodes.
[07:35] Samir: I'll own the benchmark, coordinate with infra to spin a dedicated GPU pool that mirrors prod fleet mix — A100 with driver 515 and 525, V100, etc. Plan to run by 11/25.
[07:55] Arjun: Observability gap — we need better correlation between rollout steps and per-model SLOs. Right now the tracing is per-request but not annotated with rollout-id. If we annotate traces with deployment metadata we can filter quickly.
[08:20] Emily: Good call. We'll add rollout-id in trace headers and include it in log context. That will make it immediate to pivot to affected rollout.
[08:40] Priya: Action items recap... (recap follows)
[09:00] Priya: Emily opens PR + tests; Arjun adds per-model tail-latency and KV-cache metrics; Samir runs benchmark; Jordan reverts policy and updates runbook; Nina adds regression; I'll draft external note. Any blockers?
[09:25] Cameron: From product, make sure the customer-facing note includes mitigation steps they can take (like fallback to hosted smaller concurrency or pin older model versions) and timeline for full validation.
[09:45] Grace: Support will prepare canned responses and an internal triage doc.
[10:00] Maya: Question — does this change our launch date for the new feature?
[10:10] Priya: We will delay aggressive rollout but not the public feature launch. The launch remains on track if we validate the patch and pass the benchmark by end of next week. If benchmark fails, we'll postpone.
[10:25] Samir: One more engineering note: the autoscaler flapping is an independent follow-up. We should treat it as separate ticket but expedite since it affects SLOs.
[10:40] Priya: OK create a ticket for autoscaler and prioritize P2. Samir will assign.
[10:50] Emily: I'll add details to the PR about the exact kernel selection heuristics and the driver matrix used for tests.
[11:05] Priya: Great. Any other comments?
[11:15] (silence)
[11:25] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next Tuesday for status, and all owners should post updates in the incident channel. Meeting adjourned.
[11:40] END
